newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian manufacturer prospects very good - survey.
newsitem.headline: Canadian manufacturer prospects very good - survey.

text.p: Prospects for Canadian manufacturers are very good, a quarterly survey by Statistics Canada released on Thursday showed.
"Manufacturers were highly satisfied with the level of orders received in April, and remained positive about production and employment prospects for the coming three months," it said.
"They were less concerned about the current level of finished product inventories and they may increase their work force in the next three months," the federal agency added.
"However, they are less satisfied with the number of unfilled orders on their books."

Forty percent of manufacturers said their current level of orders received was rising, up from 30 percent in the last survey, taken in January. Twelve percent said their orders were declining. Transportation equipment continued to be one of the big contributors to the positive momentum, it said.
Twenty-three percent said they expected to increase production in the coming quarter, and 16 percent planned to cut production.
Eighteen percent (four points higher than in January) felt the current level of finished products inventories was too high and 13 percent (eight points higher) thought it too low.
Fourteen percent reported a lower-than-normal backlog of unfilled orders, while seven percent said higher than normal, giving a balance of -7, down from +1 in January.
Fifteen percent said they would increase the size of their work force, and 11 percent said they would cut it, giving a balance of +4, up from +1 in January.

A shortage of skilled labor was a concern for five percent, up from three percent in the last survey. Concern about shortages of raw materials rose one point to four percent, down from the six percent recorded in April 1995. Eighty-seven percent said they have no production difficulties.
